decisions.reason: The existing same-message MODIFY captures shared right-arm derivation but omits the required clarified behavior of maintaining confidence through the final stretch before the terminal.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hi [FREELANCER_NAME_001],

Thank you for giving the terminal such thoughtful exploration. This has actually clarified something important for me.

Option 2 from the previous round remains my favorite. At this point, I don’t think my eye is focused on the terminal itself. I believe it is responding instead to the final section of the right arm just before the terminal. I’d love to explore whether that last stretch can maintain a little more confidence before it ends, allowing the gesture to carry conviction all the way through rather than becoming softer as it nears the finish.

I also feel that the project has arrived at an exciting stage. Instead of continuing to assess the capital V by itself, I’d like to begin seeing how this gesture carries into the lowercase v and the É accent. Because the right arm will ultimately define all three, viewing them together should help us determine whether we have truly established the architectural language of the complete Vellvé identity.

value_updates.right_arm_gesture_relationship: The lowercase closing v must carry the Hero V's right-arm gesture, with that right arm serving as a defining element across both forms.
value_updates.final_section_behavior_derivation: The lowercase closing v must carry the Hero V's clarified final right-arm stretch, maintaining confidence through the finish rather than becoming softer near the terminal.
